title: Align and Segment: Unsupervised Learning for Building Segmentation From Misaligned Labels
mechanism: A spatial transformer warps the misaligned label during training so the warped label is the target, with a self-supervised regulariser plus augmentation that stops the segmenter from learning the misalignment; no clean labels needed.
adaptation: Replace the affine warp with a learned per-source label renderer: the net predicts a 1 px crack centreline; a differentiable renderer (Gaussian blur with learnable width and learnable sub-pixel shift per source, 5 sources x 3 numbers) maps it to what that source's annotator draws; loss against the human label. Test: render with the cell's source parameters for strict IoU, or output the centreline for relF1@2. E1 labels are about 1.5x wider than train, so the E1 render width is a stated val-free choice.
min_experiment: Arm: centreline head + per-source renderer on house U-Net++, 5 seeds; baseline: house. Metrics: pooled crack IoU and per-source crack IoU (BMRK 0.379, CFVS-no-twin 0.397). Kill if pooled crack IoU gain < 0.012 and no source gains >= 0.02.
evidence: R: synthetic and real misaligned building labels from several cities; numbers not read (abstract-level via web listing). Code link from the same listing, not opened.
prior_overlap: none: source-conditional prediction and learned label offsets are listed as never tried in BRIEF section 5. D13 rejected AnS as affine-only; this adaptation changes the transform to per-source width and shift.

alt_notes.adaptation: Learn a small per-cell deformation field (+/-3 px, smooth) that warps crack labels to agree with the segmenter under flips and rot90; train the segmenter on the warped labels. Inactive labels are kept fixed (well labelled).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Try only after STEAL. Arm: learned warp field + house, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if there is no detectable difference.
